name: Persinger lab: right temporoparietal burst-firing (20 min)
origin: Laurentian University: Richards, Koren & Persinger 1992; Healey, Persinger & Koren 1996; Persinger & Healey 2002
summary: The right-sided arm of the Persinger lab's lateralisation study: the 230-point burst-firing pattern (3-ms points, 0.69 s) with 4 s between presentations, right side about ten times stronger, for 20 min. The lab reports a marked rise in hypnotic suggestibility only in this group (Healey 1996) and more presences, fears and odd smells than in the left or sham groups (Persinger & Healey 2002).
notes: Healey 1996 played 230 points of 3 ms for 20 min through a helmet with four solenoids per side, the field going to each left-right pair in turn, once round every 2 s; the other side had about 1/10 of the strength (pp.2-3 [202-203]). Persinger & Healey 2002 report the same 48 people, give 4 s between presentations (the pause, not the cycle) and put the side ratio at 2 to 3 to 1 (p.3 [535]). This program plays 0.69 s on and 4 s off: one left-right pair is on at a time, and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The left side plays at one tenth. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. The burst is the project's rising sweep with the published point duration and length; the point values were never published as numbers (the lab prints the shape only as a small figure). Field: Healey 1996 gives 1 to 5 uT over the activated hemisphere, place not given (p.3 [203]); Persinger & Healey 2002 give 100 nT near the midpoint and 1 uT along the inside of the helmet (p.3 [535]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Support: Healey 1996 reports a marked rise in suggestibility only in the right group (eta = 0.58). Richards 1992 (24 people, no sham group, earlier 1-ms burst): apprehension .8 (.4) for women, 0 for men with right-sided fields (pp.2-3 [668-669]). presence-right plays it on the right side only, 20 + 10 min. One lab, not repeated elsewhere. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Compare blind (right, left, persinger-burst-temporal-bilateral, sham). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop on fear, headache or distress.
setting: Partial sensory deprivation: blindfold or opaque goggles, reclining in a very quiet, darkened room. For the suggestibility test, take a standard hypnotic-susceptibility scale before and after (the lab used Spiegel's Hypnotic Induction Profile), scored by someone who does not know the condition.
schedule: One 20-min exposure per arm. At most once a week; run right, left, bilateral and sham sessions in blinded, counterbalanced order.
source: Healey, Persinger & Koren 1996, Int J Neurosci 87:201 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9003980/ ; Richards, Koren & Persinger 1992, Percept Mot Skills 75:667 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/1408634/ ; Persinger & Healey 2002, J Nerv Ment Dis 190:533 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12193838/ ; Tiller & Persinger 1994, Int J Neurosci 79:157 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7744557/ ; St-Pierre & Persinger 2006, Int J Neurosci 116:1079 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16861170/ ; Carniello 2020, PhD thesis, Laurentian University, p. 89 (230-point burst-firing file, 3-ms points) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/8c92763c-cd19-4a21-b242-3b572a28ce55 ; Collins 2014, MA thesis 'Investigating the Shiva', Laurentian University, p. 31 (289 points, 3 ms, 4000 ms) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/16d96136-680c-4afe-8044-f9137bd01afc ; Martin & Persinger 2004, Neurosci Lett 366:226 (burst-firing once every 4 s) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15276252/ ; Persinger, Hoang & Baker-Price 2009, Electromagn Biol Med 28:374 ('once every 3 s for about 0.7 s') https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20017628/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
